**project_instructions_visible** — Original `kyqualify.py:2735` used `control = codex_in_context(empty, token, "NO_PROJECT_INSTRUCTIONS")`; lines 2742–2743 used `elif control is not False: result, why = "unknown", "the empty-repository negative control is not clean"`. The repair matches the entire whitespace-normalized on-disk repository AGENTS.md inside the initial injected instruction block, and requires that block to be absent in the empty record. Missing records remain unknown. The base prompt prohibited commands: the record contains the instruction to read CLAUDE.md, but no actual CLAUDE.md read.

**user_skills_visible** — This was a true finding, not a detector bug. `runs/base/stdout.jsonl:4` names layer-value-elevation. The injected developer catalogue (base rollout line 3; real-skills-message.jsonl:1) lists that skill at `r0/layer-value-elevation/SKILL.md`, with r0 = `/Users/Dev/.codex/skills`. It also lists Codex system skills, `.agents/skills` skills, and project `.claude/skills` skills. Original `kyqualify.py:2889` used `mine = sorted(name for name in facts.get("user_skill_names") or [] if listed is not None and name in listed)`; lines 2891–2892 set `"required": False` and `"result": "unknown" if listed is None else "fail" if mine else "pass"`. It correctly reported fail.

`codex exec --help` describes --ignore-user-config as excluding config.toml only. `codex features list` includes skill_search (already disabled) and skip_host_skill_discovery (under development); it offers no universal --disable skills flag. The installed binary strings identify SkillsConfig fields bundled, include_instructions, max_context_tokens, config. `codex -c skills.include_instructions=false features list` exits 0; supplying a string for this key exits 1 with `invalid type: string ... expected a boolean in skills.include_instructions`. This verifies a real boolean config key without executing a model. Both argv builders now pass `-c skills.include_instructions=false`; the new receipt bind is skills_include_instructions=false and kyboot rejects mismatches.

**(I) INTERPRETATION:** skills.include_instructions=false suppresses the advertised skill instructions/catalogue; its real effect remains to be measured by the cockpit. It does not make skill files unreadable. The visibility check stays reported and can still fail honestly. skip_host_skill_discovery has unverified scope and is not enabled by inference from its name.

## Expected rerun and reviewer impact

Offline replay of all original runs with the repaired detectors yields pass for all required checks except network (unknown without --control); user_skills_visible remains fail. No forbidden canary effect or git/config/hook change was observed. Expect a real builder PASS if the allowed-network control succeeds, session records are present and parseable, and all other required/negative probes repeat successfully. Unsupported wrapper syntax or absent outputs remains unknown. The two job-rooted reviewer configurations share the wrapper, outside/tmp and network issues; item read/write now also consume the paired rollout result. Their project-instruction check remains reported rather than required. Skill suppression applies identically to builder and reviewers.

The qualification fake is now `fake_codex_qualify.py`, loaded by test_kyqualify_codex.py. It emits both native command_execution events and rollout-only exec calls, the actual sandbox_policy.type shape, injected global/project instruction blocks, and an item-level warning. Unsafe /tmp-leak testing uses an injected observed effect in the real judge instead of creating a physical file outside the test rig. Claude qualification behavior is unchanged.
